_about: The claim and warrant vocabulary. tools/query/export_rdf.py writes the OWL file from this, and web/build-atlas.mjs writes the /vocabulary page from it. The namespace below is the one place to change it. It is registered at w3id.org (perma-id/w3id.org PR #7091, merged 2026-11-06).
title: The Symbolic World: claims and warrants
definition_note: These terms describe what the atlas records about a claim: where it rests, whose voice it is in, how much confidence its record carries, and which checks it passed. They build on PROV-O. They say nothing about Jung's concepts: there is no class hierarchy over the nodes, no domain or range on any relation of the graph, no transitivity, and nothing is inferred from a node's type.

classes.label: Node
classes.comment: A named thing in the graph. Its type is a coarse label, and nothing is inferred from it.

classes.label: Relation
classes.comment: One stored edge: a subject, a relation and an object. It carries the family. The rdf:predicate is the effective relation, which is the normalized form where one exists.

classes.label: Claim
classes.comment: One statement backed by one passage. A relation has one claim per citation, and the gate rules on each claim separately.

classes.label: Reference
classes.comment: The place a claim rests on: a volume and a paragraph of the Collected Works. The export does not carry the quoted words, which are on the concept page for the claim.

classes.label: Stage
classes.comment: One recorded step of the pipeline, dated where the record gives a date.

classes.label: Proposal
classes.comment: The step in which a model drafted a claim or a normalized form. For a claim it is the mining batch, linked by prov:wasGeneratedBy, and sw:attributionSource says whether a batch record or the documented procedure names the proposer. Claims whose audit names no batch have none.

classes.label: Gate check
classes.comment: A model of a different family from the proposer judged the paragraph against the claim, or a normalized form against its claim.

classes.label: Cross-vendor audit
classes.comment: A model from another company judged the work again. The verdict is the one the record gives. Where the record gives none, the export gives none.

classes.label: Family assignment
classes.comment: An assignment of a relation to a family, or a record that none was settled. A family is assigned when the two arms agree or a person rules. Some assignments also carry an audit by the calibrated family gate, given in sw:familyAudit.

classes.label: Voice
classes.comment: Whose voice the claim is in. This is a separate question from whether the claim is true.

classes.label: Commitment
classes.comment: The confidence recorded for the claim, from the confidence field of its reference: high, medium or low. A later check can lower it, as an audit or a dispute has done for some claims.

classes.label: Rung
classes.comment: A warrant: the backing a part of a claim has. The rungs have no order in this vocabulary, because passing one warrants nothing about another.

classes.label: Family state
classes.comment: Where a relation stands in the family layer.

individuals.label: Jung reports a parallel
individuals.comment: Jung reports someone else's material as a parallel.

individuals.label: Jung quotes a source
individuals.comment: Jung quotes a source, and the claim names it.

individuals.label: High commitment
individuals.comment: The reference records its confidence as high.

individuals.label: Medium commitment
individuals.comment: The reference records its confidence as medium. A reference recorded as lowered from high to medium also lands here, with the original string kept beside it.

individuals.label: Low commitment
individuals.comment: The reference records its confidence as low.

individuals.label: Attested
individuals.comment: The quote is in the paragraph. It settles only that the words are in the book.

individuals.label: Model-supported
individuals.comment: A gate of a different family from the proposer passed the claim.

individuals.label: Cross-checked
individuals.comment: A model from another company judged the claim again. Read the audit's verdict beside this rung.

individuals.label: Normalized
individuals.comment: The relation has a short normalized form beside the frozen wording.

individuals.label: Family-assigned
individuals.comment: The relation is filed under a family. It inherits nothing from the verification of the claim beneath it.

individuals.label: Derived
individuals.comment: A row produced at query time by a declared inverse or symmetry rule. Derived rows are never stored, so this rung has no instances in the export.

individuals.label: Human-reviewed
individuals.comment: One person judged it. The review records sit outside the graph's source data, so this export reports no instances.

individuals.label: Human-agreed
individuals.comment: Two people judged it independently. No item in the graph has reached this rung.

individuals.label: Pending adjudication
individuals.comment: The arms disagreed, and the relation waits for a person to rule.

individuals.label: Text undecided
individuals.comment: The text does not decide between families.

annotation_properties.label: recorded as
annotation_properties.comment: The string the graph's source data stores for this individual.

object_properties.label: has evidence
object_properties.comment: The place the claim rests on.

object_properties.label: voice
object_properties.comment: Whose voice the claim is in.

object_properties.label: commitment
object_properties.comment: The confidence recorded for the claim.

object_properties.label: reached rung
object_properties.comment: A rung the record shows this claim or relation has reached. Absence means the record does not show it.

object_properties.label: checked by
object_properties.comment: A recorded stage that acted on this claim or relation.

object_properties.label: family
object_properties.comment: The family this relation is filed under, named by its super-property. The assignment belongs to the edge, not to the relation string.

object_properties.label: family state
object_properties.comment: Where the relation stands in the family layer.

object_properties.label: verbatim relation
object_properties.comment: The frozen wording the gate judged, where a normalized form replaced it as the effective relation. The export does not carry it, because a long predicate can repeat the source's words.

datatype_properties.label: node type
datatype_properties.comment: The node's coarse type label, as recorded.

datatype_properties.label: volume
datatype_properties.comment: The volume of the Collected Works, as recorded: 9i, 14.

datatype_properties.label: quote
datatype_properties.comment: The quoted words. The export does not carry them, and a switch in the exporter can write them to a separate file outside the CC BY grant.

datatype_properties.label: voice source
datatype_properties.comment: The source named for the claim's voice, as recorded.

datatype_properties.label: confidence as recorded
datatype_properties.comment: The original confidence string, given where it is a downgrade rather than a single level.

datatype_properties.label: verdict
datatype_properties.comment: The audit's verdict as recorded. Older audits use different words, and the export keeps them as they are.

datatype_properties.label: batch
datatype_properties.comment: The mining batch named in a stage: the batch an audit names, or the batch a proposal is.

datatype_properties.label: audit record
datatype_properties.comment: The audit record as stored. The agent, date, verdict and batch here are read from this string.

datatype_properties.label: proposer as recorded
datatype_properties.comment: The words that name the proposer, as the source gives them: a model id, or a family such as Opus-family miner subagent.

datatype_properties.label: attribution source
datatype_properties.comment: Where the proposer comes from: record, when a batch record names it, or procedure, when only the documented mining procedure does.

datatype_properties.label: assigned by
datatype_properties.comment: How the family was assigned, as recorded: the two arms agreeing, or a person ruling.

datatype_properties.label: family audit
datatype_properties.comment: The calibrated gate's audit of the assignment, as recorded.
